```{python}
#| echo: false
import html
import json
from pathlib import Path

T = Path("../results/tables")
CAL = json.loads((T / "rollout_calendar.json").read_text("utf-8"))
ROWS = [row for row in CAL["items"] if row["reader"]]
```

arrive with the first month of winter data.

## What this page is waiting for

I fixed the tests on `{python} ROWS[0]["when"]`, before opening any fire
data. The winter itself arrives a month at a time. Each row below is
something this site is waiting for, when I expect it, and what changes here
when it comes. The dates are when the data is expected to be published, not
promises.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
lines = ['<ol class="timetable">']
for row in ROWS:
    state = ' class="done"' if row["done"] else ""
    lines.append(
        f'<li{state} data-end="{row["end"]}"><i class="st"></i>'
        f'<span class="num">{html.escape(row["when"])}</span>'
        f'<span class="what">{html.escape(row["title"])}<span class="chip">next</span></span>'
        f'<span class="then">{html.escape(row["site_change"])}</span></li>')
lines.append("</ol>")
print("```{=html}\n" + "\n".join(lines) + "\n```")
```

```{=html}
<script>
// The next row is the first one not yet done whose date has not passed, as of
// the visitor's own day. Done marks come from the build, never from the clock.
(function () {
  var today = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);
  var rows = document.querySelectorAll("ol.timetable > li");
  for (var i = 0; i < rows.length; i++) {
    if (!rows[i].classList.contains("done") && rows[i].dataset.end >= today) {
      rows[i].classList.add("next");
      break;
    }
  }
})();
</script>
```

A filled dot is something already in this site's files. A date that has
passed with an open dot means the data came late or I have not rebuilt the
page yet.
